cohort: 197 post-delivery women suspected with puerperal sepsis admitted at Muhimbili National Hospital
finding: Puerperal sepsis was mostly caused by E. coli and Klebsiella spp., which exhibited very high levels of resistance to most antibiotics used in empiric treatment.
mod_finding: 50.3% of participants had spontaneous vaginal delivery, while 49.2% had caesarean section.
